verdict.rationale: Lithic ships an official MCP server, so a connected AI assistant (Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot) can search docs, inspect schemas and execute live API requests. Lithic's blog shows natural-language-driven workflows such as creating a virtual card, configuring authorization rules and running transactions. Natural-language operation depends on a third-party AI client, and there is no native natural-language interface in the product itself. Missing for 10: a native in-product natural-language interface, independent or hands-on corroboration of MCP-driven operation, and documentation of coverage limits and safety controls for agent-executed live calls.
